title: How the Palace Commits
idiom: hand-coloured Dutch canal-engineering etching, many barges and one lock gate
hero_prompt: Hand-coloured etching in the manner of an 18th-century Dutch canal-engineering plate, hand-made on paper, flat and graphic with visible etched line and watercolour texture, not a photograph, not a 3D render, no depth-of-field, wide panoramic composition: three narrow side canals curving in from the left, each with a small wooden barge waiting in single file, all converging on one stout wooden lock gate set in a stone wall, with a single barge passing through it into a broad calm main canal on the right; a woman lock-keeper in a long apron stands on the gate's beam, leaning on the long balance arm; on the bank beside her stands a tall curved brass listening horn on a post, its wide mouth turned toward the water, and far down the main canal a second lock gate stands shut. Washes of slate blue, sand and muted green.
icon_prompt: Linocut emblem, a flat single-colour black silhouette on a teal ground, no shading or gradients: three curved channels on the left narrowing together into one straight channel that passes between two thick stone gate posts. Bold, high-contrast, no fine linework, reads clearly at 24 pixels.
